title: Launching Your First EC2 Instance 🚀
description: Hands‑on walkthrough from console click to a live web server.

slides.title: Step 1: Choose an AMI 🖼️
slides.content:
# Let’s Launch!

Go to EC2 Dashboard → **Launch Instance** → **Launch instance**.

1. **Name**: Give your instance a tag, e.g., `My-First-WebServer`.
2. **Application and OS Images**: Select **Amazon Linux 2023 AMI** (Free Tier eligible). It’s the first option, marked 'Free tier eligible'.
3. Leave architecture as **64-bit (x86)**.

slides.title: Step 2: Instance Type & Key Pair 🔑
slides.content:
# Pick Hardware & Login

4. **Instance type**: Choose **t2.micro** (Free Tier).
5. **Key pair**: Create new or select existing. If new, give it a name, download the `.pem` file. Store it safely.

> Without a key pair you won’t be able to SSH. Don’t skip this step.

slides.title: Step 3: Network Settings 🌐
slides.content:
# Firewall Configuration

6. Click **Edit** in Network settings.
7. **VPC**: select the default VPC.
8. **Subnet**: any AZ (leave default).
9. **Auto‑assign public IP**: Enable (so you can reach it).
10. **Firewall (security groups)**: Choose **Create security group**.
    - Add a rule for **SSH** (port 22) – restrict source to 'My IP' for safety.
    - Add a rule for **HTTP** (port 80) – source 'Anywhere' (0.0.0.0/0) so the web server is reachable.
11. Leave storage as default (30 GB gp2, Free Tier eligible).

quizData.question: Why should the SSH source be restricted to 'My IP'?

options.text: Because SSH doesn’t work from other IPs
To prevent attackers from brute‑forcing your instance

quizData.explanation: Restricting SSH to your IP prevents the entire internet from attempting to log in, drastically reducing security risk.

slides.title: Step 4: Launch & Connect 📡
slides.content:
# Start the Instance

12. Review and click **Launch instance**.
13. Wait until the instance state is 'Running' and 'Status check' passes.
14. Select the instance, find its **Public IPv4 address** in the details tab.
15. Open a terminal (or use EC2 Instance Connect) and SSH:
```bash
ssh -i your-key.pem ec2-user@<public-ip>
```

slides.title: Step 5: Install a Web Server 🌐
slides.content:
# Your First Live Site Once logged in, run these commands to install Apache: ```bash sudo yum update -y sudo yum install -y httpd sudo systemctl start httpd sudo systemctl enable httpd echo '

Hello from EC2!

' | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html ``` Now visit your instance’s public IP in a browser. You should see 'Hello from EC2!'. 🎉

slides.title: Pro Tip: User Data 🚀
slides.content:
## Automate at Launch

You can paste a shell script into **User data** during launch (under Advanced details). The script runs once at first boot. Put the Apache install commands there, and your web server is ready right after launch – no manual SSH needed for setup.
